sections.content:
You know passive *se* from B1 Unit 6 and the *ser* passive from B1 Unit 18. In diplomatic and geopolitical prose, passive *se* extends well beyond simple-present rules into compound tenses and modal periphrases to report agreements, sanctions and corridors without repeating the institutional actors.

In compound tenses and modals, the finite verb still agrees with the grammatical subject: *se han suscrito convenios bilaterales*, *se deben proteger los corredores*. With modal + infinitive, *se* may precede the modal (*se pueden ampliar las rutas*) or attach to the infinitive (*pueden ampliarse las rutas*), and the modal agrees with the plural noun in both positions.

Standard formal writing avoids adding a *por* agent to passive *se*. When the diplomatic actor must be named, switch to *ser* + participle: *el convenio fue suscrito por ambos bloques*, not *se suscribió por ambos bloques*.

sections.title: Passive *se* at C1 density
rows: *se ha suscrito un convenio* / *se han suscrito dos convenios*
*la alianza fue ratificada por los socios* (avoid *se ratificó por*)

items.spanish: Durante la cumbre se han suscrito tres convenios de cooperación bilateral.
items.english: During the summit, three bilateral cooperation agreements have been signed.

items.spanish: Se deben modernizar los corredores ferroviarios antes de ampliar el comercio.
items.english: The rail corridors must be modernised before expanding trade.

items.spanish: Pueden abrirse nuevas rutas multilaterales si mejora la estabilidad regional.
items.english: New multilateral routes can be opened if regional stability improves.

items.spanish: El convenio fue suscrito por los representantes de ambos bloques.
items.english: The agreement was signed by the representatives of both blocs.

sections.content: Check verb agreement when the plural subject comes after the verb (*se han suscrito convenios*, not *se ha suscrito convenios*), and switch to *ser* + participle whenever a *por* agent appears.
